messages.subject: Semi-aquatic endotherm
parts:
Hi Mike & Fellow Energetics Fans

I was very excited to see today that the endotherm model is now available in NicheMapR. I am thinking of including it in an upcoming project but looking at the paper, its use is described for 'most types of terrestrial animal'. So can it be applied to an aquatic air breathing animal (specifically a seabird)? The original Niche Mapper software has been applied to seabirds (https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.032300). But can NicheMapR be applied in the same way for a bird semi-submerged in water? 

Best wishes

Jon

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Semi-aquatic endotherm
parts:
Hi Jon,

Yes it can in that you can make the 'fluid' air or water (input argument 'FLTYPE') though to make e.g. the ventral side water and the top side air you'd have to make some modifications to the endoR_devel function so that the fluid type changes between the dorsal and ventral calls to SIMULSOL.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Semi-aquatic endotherm
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

It is, in that you just need to add:

        if(S == 2){
          FLTYPE <- 2
        }else{
          FLTYPE <- 0
        }

to endoR_devel, in addition to passing the appropriate values for sea water for the environmental conditions, but I would strongly recommend having a clear understanding of exactly what the model is doing before proceeding, and ideally having some good test data to compare against. Definitely step through the tutorials.

All the best,
Mike
